title: orchestrate.py plan crashes with ENAMETOOLONG on MCP config
source_context: SnapWizard project in ~/Projects/screenshot, plan command with ~1500 char description
description: Running 'orchestrate.py plan' with a long project description fails: 'Claude failed: Error: Invalid MCP configuration: Failed to read file: Error: ENAMETOOLONG'. Looks like the project description (or a path built from it) is passed where a file path is expected, or the MCP config path is constructed from the prompt text.
proposed_changes: Check how the claude -p subprocess gets its --mcp-config argument; likely the description string leaks into a file path. Write the plan prompt to a temp file instead of inlining it.

triage.evidence: scripts/orchestrate.py lines 786-797 (current HEAD): cmd.extend(["--mcp-config", mcp_config]) ... cmd.append(safe_prompt) — prompt directly follows the variadic --mcp-config option with no intervening flag. git log: last commit to orchestrate.py is c09b11b dated 2026-07-03, before the 2026-07-14 report; grep shows no ENAMETOOLONG handling or temp-file workaround anywhere in scripts/.
triage.note: Bug still present and root cause confirmed. In claude_prompt() the positional prompt is appended immediately after the variadic --mcp-config flag, so Claude CLI consumes the long prompt as an extra MCP config value, fails JSON parse, treats it as a file path, and dies with ENAMETOOLONG — exactly the reported crash, length-dependent as described. orchestrate.py has not been touched since 2026-07-03 (proposal filed 2026-07-14), so no fix has landed. Fix is a small argument-ordering change (separate the prompt from --mcp-config with a non-variadic flag or option terminator) and does not involve scripts/prometheus.py. Same latent pattern exists at delegate.py:2494 but is out of this proposal's declared scope.
